summary: Building a complete Node.js bookstore API with SQLite from an empty repo requires a data contract (schema), API contract (routes), and comprehensive implementation—feature_with_architecture loop fits because this creates new API and data contracts in a repo with no existing application code.

steps.why: Extract structured requirements from the detailed acceptance criteria.
steps.instructions: Keep the requirements focused on the API contract, data model, and behavioral rules; the ticket already provides clear acceptance criteria.

steps.why: Define the SQLite schema, Express route contracts, auth model, and cart/checkout state transitions before coding.
steps.instructions: Design the complete data model (product, cart, cart_item, order, order_item tables with constraints), API surface (all routes with request/response shapes), role-based access rules, and cart-to-order state machine; address concurrency for stock updates.

steps.why: Break down into implementable slices: scaffold, schema, each API endpoint group, and tests.
steps.instructions: Structure stories so the first delivers the project scaffold and schema, then catalog endpoints, then cart, then checkout and shipping, then comprehensive tests; each story should be independently testable.

steps.why: Each story needs a concrete file plan and implementation detail for the endpoints, database access, and validation logic.
steps.instructions: Provide file structures, Express route handler skeletons, SQL queries for each operation, and validation rules; ensure better-sqlite3 usage patterns and transaction boundaries are explicit.

steps.why: Map each acceptance criterion to specific test cases covering happy paths, auth, validation, and edge cases.
steps.instructions: Create tests for health check, catalog auth (admin/shopper), cart operations (add/update/delete), checkout with stock validation, shipping auth, and persistence across restarts; ensure traceability to every acceptance criterion.

steps.why: Verify consistency between the schema in HLD, the API contracts in HLD, the route implementations in stories, and the test coverage.
steps.instructions: Check that every table in the schema appears in stories, every route in the HLD has implementation detail in a story, and every acceptance criterion has a corresponding test case.

steps.why: Pack per-ticket specs into merged_plan.md for review.
Human approval of specs and this plan before Dev.

skipped.why: The ticket clearly defines scope, acceptance criteria, and what is out of scope; no product ambiguity exists.
